FONTLOG for CPGothic UI JP
==========================

This file provides detailed information on the CPGothic UI JP font software.
This information should be distributed along with the CPGothic UI JP fonts and
any derivative works.


Basic Font Information
----------------------

CPGothic UI JP is the user-interface typeface compiled into the CrossPoint
Reader Japanese firmware for the Xteink X4. It is a subset of UDEV Gothic,
containing only the characters the firmware's own fixed interface strings need
-- 351 non-ASCII characters plus ASCII -- rasterised at six point sizes
(8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18) into the firmware image itself.

It is **not** a general-purpose font. It cannot render a book, a filename or an
author's name, and it is not installable on a computer. Body text on the device
is drawn from a font the reader installs on the SD card; UDEV Gothic itself is
what we recommend there, unmodified and under its own name.

UDEV Gothic was chosen because it is a universal-design face: `l` and `I`, `O`
and `0` are distinguishable, which matters on a 480x800 electrophoretic panel
at 8 pt.


Why the name changed
--------------------

UDEV Gothic carries a Reserved Font Name. A subset is a Modified Version, so
the Reserved Font Name may not be used for it:

  "it is not possible to preserve FE, and so pre-subsetting needs to be
   considered a Modified Version for which RFN restrictions apply."
  -- https://openfontlicense.org/webfonts-and-reserved-font-names/

  "be creative and avoid names that reuse almost all the same letters in the
   same order or sound like the original. It will help everyone if Original
   Versions and Modified Versions can easily be distinguished from one another
   and from other derivatives."
  -- https://openfontlicense.org/how-to-modify-ofl-fonts/

"CPGothic UI JP" carries no part of "UDEV", and does not sound like it. CP is
the firmware, UI is what the font is for, JP is the language it covers.
"Gothic" is the ordinary classification term for a sans-serif Japanese face
(ゴシック体), used across the family of such fonts; the name the OFL reserves
is the primary font name presented to users, which is "UDEV Gothic".

Provenance is recorded here and in the copyright notices rather than in the
name, which is what the guidance asks for.


Acknowledgements
----------------

(No acknowledgement is required by the licence. It is offered because these
fonts are the work of other people.)

CPGothic UI JP is a subset of UDEV Gothic by Yuko OTAWARA, which is itself a
composition of two faces:

  BIZ UDGothic   -- the Japanese characters. A universal-design face by
                    Morisawa, released by the BIZ UDGothic Project Authors.
  JetBrains Mono -- the Latin letters and digits, by JetBrains.

Our thanks to all three.

Copyright 2022 The BIZ UDGothic Project Authors
  (https://github.com/googlefonts/morisawa-biz-ud-gothic)
Copyright 2020 The JetBrains Mono Project Authors
  (https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono)

All three are licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1, whose text
accompanies this file as OFL-1.1.txt.

Note for redistributors: the UDEV Gothic release archive contains the TTF files
only -- no licence text. OFL clause 2 requires the copyright notice and the
licence to travel with every copy, so the text has to be taken from the project
repository and bundled, as it is here.


ChangeLog
---------

<date of release>  CPGothic UI JP  (CrossPoint Reader JP)
- Subset of UDEV Gothic Regular v2.0.0 to the 351 non-ASCII characters used by
  the firmware's fixed interface strings, plus ASCII.
- Rasterised to 2-bit bitmaps at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 pt and compiled into
  the firmware image. No outlines are redistributed.
- Renamed, for the reason given above.


Information for Contributors
----------------------------

CPGothic UI JP is generated, not edited: see scripts/gen_ui_charset.py for the
character set and lib/EpdFont/scripts/fontconvert.py for the rasteriser. To
change which characters it holds, change the interface strings in
lib/I18n/translations/japanese.yaml and regenerate.

UDEV Gothic is at https://github.com/yuru7/udev-gothic and is the place to
contribute to the outlines.
